- **Items or steps:** 12 steps. They run 34 to 147 words (the panel cover, 37; the interlock plate and cover holes, 147, the longest); typical 90 to 110 words, 30 to 40 seconds. Order: open the panel and size the job first (30 or 50 amps from a measured storm-night load), then the outside half (the inlet's place, the hole), then the cable into the panel, then the inlet wired, then the panel wiring, then the interlock, and only then why it matters.
- **Promise devices:** a question promised and paid (30 or 50 amps, asked at 0:56, answered at 3:44); the interlock promised at 0:43 as "a critical component" and its reason held to the end (10:22); a check at home in effect (the list of what must run on a storm night). No step count, no myth flag, no priority flag.
- **Forward lines:** 4 (0:37, 1:06, 4:26, 9:02). Longest gap between a forward line or payoff: about 4:30 (4:33-9:02, the cable and inlet wiring).
- **Stakes:** almost none until 10:22. Then two plain consequences, each said once: the inlet's exposed pins live with both breakers on, and back-feed onto the line for the utility crews. In proportion, but late, and nothing on fire, shock at the panel or carbon monoxide.
- **Safety lines:** call-a-professional lines at 0:22 (50 words) and 1:10 (42 words), both with comfort as the trigger. No power-off and no verify-dead line anywhere: the cover comes off and the clamp goes on the service conductors with the house running (0:45, 1:21), and the panel wiring at 8:28 never says the main is off. Torque to the maker's figure twice (8:02, 8:57).
- **CTA placement:** a store link at 4:00 (92 words, about 26 seconds, at 32% of the video); at the end, an open feedback ask (36 words) and a plug for another video (54 words).
- **Ending:** installed and ready, the generator tests to come, the comment ask, the video plug, sign-off. No recap, no storm-night order and no test of the lockout on camera.
- **What sets it apart from other models of its type:**
  - The job is sized before any wiring: a measured storm-night load (furnace, sump pump, lights, one burner) decides 30 or 50 amps. For us that's a list the viewer makes of what must run, never a meter on the service wires.
  - The why of the interlock comes last, as a question with two plain consequences (live pins on the inlet; back-feed onto the line for the workers). It's the clearest mechanism of the three generator how-tos (E02, E33, E34).
  - It opens with permission to watch only to learn the steps, as an informed customer of a licensed electrician: the nearest any model comes to our scope line. The body then breaks it, with all of the panel work done by the presenter.

## Why it works

The comments are from people who did it or are about to, and they add what the video left out. The most-liked viewer comment is a sizing tip: "I would suggest you always install a 50A input plug even if you only use a small generator and a 30A breaker, so you have the option to use a larger generator down the road." (91 likes). Then a safety extra, "The one extra thing I did was to include a power back on alarm." (75 likes), and a storm story: "Little did I know that effort would save my tail less than 2 weeks later with IAN." (44 likes). The complaints are about what wasn't shown: "I think you should have shown how and where to install the generator breaker so it would interface with the interlock." (48 likes) and "every generator interlock video shows an ideal situation with a perfect QO or Siemens panel with a simple interlock" (25 likes). One viewer takes exactly the angle our channel takes: "You explained very well and at least I know the concept if I need to hire someone to install." (9 likes). The opening gives the wish and the outage in 20 seconds, then the scope; the pace is easy (about 179 words a minute). What viewers did after: they describe their own generator sizes, transfer switches and alarms in the replies.

## Doesn't transfer

- **Greeting with a name:** [0:00] "how's it going you guys it's Scott with"
- **No power-off and no verify-dead line anywhere; the panel cover comes off and the meter goes on with the house running:** [0:45] "so I'm going to start off by taking the cover off" and [1:24] "I'm going to do is I'm going to take my two conductors my main conductors coming in from my meter base". For Frederick nothing behind the dead front is the viewer's, and a measurement on the service conductors is never narrated: the load list is said as what the viewer plans to run, from the brief.
- **The panel half of the job is the presenter's own work inside the panel:** [5:16] "now up at our load Center or the panel I'll go ahead and take out that knockout"; [8:30] "we'll start off with the neutral in the ground and since it's the main electrical panel those will both land on the same bus bars"; [9:05] "we'll remove this bolt and then place a retaining bracket on that 30 amp breaker". For Frederick this is the licensed electrician's part, put in with a permit: the script says what the electrician fits and why, and gives the homeowner the load list, the storm-night order and the generator's place outdoors.
- **No carbon monoxide line, nothing on where the generator stands, and no storm-night order** (the video ends at the install): [11:39] "I'm ready to go I'm gonna be testing out some gen sets in the future". Every Frederick script with a running generator says both, from facts guide §11 (11.1 to 11.7).
- **Comfort as the call-a-professional trigger** (vague): [1:13] "feel comfortable doing this do not approach this project call in a professional". Ours names the trigger: the generator connection itself is the electrician's.
- **His own house and loads as the proof:** [2:49] "lights are now on I'm powering up my laptop" and [3:25] "what is my sump pump load I know my sump pump load is 8 amps"
- **Money and store links** (no money framing on this channel): [4:03] "down in the description and you'll see the link to our Amazon store"; [7:58] "screwdriver there's a pretty cheap one for thirty dollars"; [12:03] "want to see a really cost effective way"
- **Brand names** (say the part type from the brief): [5:42] "up with my 3M Super 33 electrical tape" and [11:45] "I do have my eyes on the ecoflow Delta"
- **Pointing at the footage:** [1:30] "left hand side here" and [12:11] "check out this video right here"
- **Possible slips (check against the brief):**
  - [10:43] "so if the main was on and also your 30 amp for your generator in that was on those problems would be electrified" ("problems" is a caption slip for "prongs": the inlet's pins)
  - [6:41] "screwdriver and my clients to tap that" (a caption slip, probably a pliers brand)
  - [3:18] "in about 17.5 amps going through the left hand side" (one house's reading on one day; sizing comes from the brief, and the 91-like comment argues for a 50 amp inlet anyway)
  - Nothing on the generator's neutral-to-ground bond (the same gap as E02) and nothing on a permit.
